claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on a constrained basis because aggregate readiness passes, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the 8% rollout with rollback/monitoring makes certification supportable so long as the exposed loan-modification-support limitation is explicitly disclosed.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the policy threshold is satisfied at launch, not merely that it could be satisfied later.
Treat readiness, limited rollout percentage, rollback, and monitoring as supportive but not sufficient when the affected segment remains exposed.
Require either exclusion of the affected use case, or reviewed risk acceptance, or clear evidence that the policy's disclosure requirement for the named use case has been completed before launch.
Downgrade when the actor's recommendation depends on a future disclosure or approval that is not in evidence.
evidence_requests: Final model-card or launch materials showing the loan modification support limitation is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Approved risk acceptance naming the loan modification support exposure and explaining why continued exposure is acceptable, if disclosure is not the sole control.
Launch-gating evidence showing the affected use case is excluded from rollout, if that is the intended mitigation path.
Approval artifact linking certification to the disclosed limitation and confirming reviewers accepted the launch on that basis.
specific_concerns: The affected loan modification support segment remains in the initial rollout cohort and is below target on hardship-document checklisting.
The available risk acceptance record is only a draft, has no approver, and does not mention the exposed segment.
The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate this weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has actually been prepared, reviewed, or attached to launch approval.
The actor's packet relies on disclosure as the key compliance bridge, but that bridge is asserted rather than evidenced.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently supportable rather than merely potentially supportable if disclosure is completed before launch.
That rollout controls plus rollback materially cure the policy problem while the affected segment remains exposed.
Any implication that monitoring and reversible rollout alone justify certification absent exclusion or approved risk acceptance.
